question: Does the 687-cell numeric reference reproduce the upper classes and lower codes printed on the 1979 chart, and which consumers depend on disagreements?
outcome: V2.1: 687 cells, eight primary codes and two upper classes corrected; 16 old lower-code ambiguities provisionally resolved. Twenty-two rows change values or alternatives and 36 numeric records change including confidence. Thirty-three cells are medium, 654 high. Reviewer final 63-cell blind reading matches; whole-chart pixel sweep supports the added class correction with no code disagreement. Direct joins affect 11 v1 and eight v3 reference units; v2 has zero direct changes and 18 unlocated units. Release chart: 36 rows; stored prediction alternatives: 72/100 v1/v2, including rank metadata.
challenge: Fifteen of 21 first-pass differences were reader errors; 630 cells initially had one reading. The whole-chart review found a shared class-85 misread despite valid class order. Worn 5/6/8 outlines require lower confidence; candidate identities and one v3 location conflict remain unresolved.
remedy: Preserved v2 and reviewer outputs, inspected native pixels for class 86, created v2.1 with dated logs and 33 medium labels, reused 63 blind readings and whole-chart pixel checks, and generated separately named impact and verification outputs. No expert review or new scores.
retry_when: An expert can confirm medium digits including class 86, 360, 208, 698 and the unresolved 734/300 cases; consumer owners can resolve unlocated identities and the v3 58/0 conflict before new versioned scoring and release snapshots.
